evals.prompt: I'm the VP Sales at Loamfield, a 22-person seed-stage B2B SaaS doing about $1.6M ARR with four AEs. Our CRM is a swamp, nobody can tell me what actually closed last month, and I lose a day a week rebuilding reports by hand. Finance froze all hiring except engineering through Q1. Write me a job description for a Revenue Operations Manager so I'm ready to post the second the freeze lifts.
evals.expected_output: A profile-choice analysis that deletes both in-house options (hiring freeze plus sub-$3M ARR), states the ordering of the remaining options out loud, and recommends a fractional operator or scoped agency project instead of the requested job description.
expectations: Runs the profile-choice test before producing any job description
States that both in-house options are deleted outright rather than ranked last, and names the hiring freeze as one reason
Names the roughly $3M ARR fractional floor as a second, independent reason the in-house options are deleted
States the ordering of the remaining options out loud rather than implying it by list order
Ranks the options by value returned per hour the hiring manager and panel spend
Recommends a fractional operator or a scoped agency project rather than a full-time requisition
Notes that four AEs sits below the roughly-five-rep threshold that precedes a first dedicated ops hire
Names at least one re-ranking against Loamfield's own specific context
States that the guidance below the ARR floor is to stay fractional, not to hire a junior instead
Does not recommend hiring a junior analyst as a cheaper substitute for the manager requisition
Does not deliver a finished job description as the primary deliverable

evals.prompt: Bramwell Tools, Series B, 140 people, 18 AEs, 6 marketers, 5 CS. Our board deck and the marketing dashboard have never once agreed on how many opportunities we sourced, and leads sit for days between marketing calling them qualified and sales actually working them. The CEO sponsors this and it reports to the CRO, headcount is approved, funded at manager level, we want a lasting capability, and there's no hard deadline. I want to hire a Salesforce administrator. Draft the scorecard.
evals.expected_output: A challenge to the systems-administrator framing, an archetype diagnosis routing reporting-trust pain to the analyst and cross-boundary handoff pain to the strategist, archetype and level named in writing, then a mission plus ranked dated outcomes and 4-6 competencies written around problems rather than tools.
expectations: Challenges the systems-administrator framing and diagnoses the archetype from the described pain rather than from the requested title
Routes reporting-trust pain to the analyst archetype and cross-boundary handoff pain to the strategist, naming the routing rule
Names the archetype and the level in writing before drafting the scorecard
States the profile-choice ordering out loud and names which options were deleted, or states that none were
Warns that most failed RevOps hires are an archetype mismatch rather than a competence failure
Writes the role definition around problems and outcomes rather than around named tools
Produces a one-line mission plus between three and eight ranked outcomes, each carrying a date
Makes each outcome objective and observable rather than an activity description
Defines between four and six competencies
Confirms the reporting line and executive sponsor are locked before the role definition is drafted
Does not set a vendor administrator certification as a must-have for this requisition

evals.prompt: Halverstad Media, 90 people. The problem sits entirely inside marketing: our marketing automation platform's routing rules were built by a contractor who left, form fills drop into the wrong nurture track, and the field mapping between the automation platform and the CRM drifts every few weeks. Sales says their pipeline is fine and they have no complaints. Our VP Marketing wants to hire a RevOps Manager to clean this up. Give me the interview loop.
evals.expected_output: A scope check identifying the pain as confined to one function, a statement that this is Marketing Ops rather than RevOps, a redirect of the requisition, and profile-choice options for the correctly scoped role - not a RevOps interview loop.
expectations: Applies the scope check before any ranking and identifies the pain as confined inside a single function
States that pain confined inside one function belongs to Marketing Ops rather than RevOps
Cites the rule that RevOps is hired when revenue problems cross team boundaries
Recommends re-scoping the requisition to a marketing operations role rather than building a RevOps loop
Names the marketing-ops-to-RevOps handoff as living in the field mapping and the data sync between the two systems
Does not produce a full RevOps interview loop as if the requisition were correctly scoped
Distinguishes this from BizOps, described as board decks, market sizing and diligence work rather than CRM ownership
Offers the profile-choice options for the correctly scoped role rather than assuming a requisition
States the ordering of those options out loud
Notes that a scoped agency project fits a single bounded fix such as rebuilding routing rules
Flags the missing executive sponsor and reporting line before any requisition proceeds

evals.prompt: Quennel Systems, 34 people, just signed a Series A term sheet. Our CRM is barely configured, half the fields are blank and reps still quote from spreadsheets. I'm the founder and I want to hire a Head of Revenue Operations at director level, because I want someone strategic who can own the whole revenue engine. They'd report jointly to me and my two co-founders. Write the role definition and the interview loop.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to draft the packet until one VP-or-C-level sponsor is committed in writing, a diagnosis of the request as an aspirational wrong-altitude hire, the real pain named as capacity plus systems, the cost of the mistake quantified with time-to-fill and ramp figures, and a ranked profile-choice recommendation instead.
expectations: Refuses to proceed to the role definition until a single VP-or-C-level executive sponsor is committed in writing
Flags the joint reporting line to three founders as an unclear-mandate failure and requires one named owner
Names executive sponsorship as the single biggest predictor of first-hire success
Identifies the requested director-level strategist as an aspirational hire mismatched to a barely configured CRM
Diagnoses the actual pain as capacity plus systems and points at a hands-on generalist or fractional help rather than a Head-of title
Describes the wrong-altitude failure as too senior to do the work and too junior to own the strategy
Names the roughly $3M ARR fractional floor or the equivalent company-size guidance as a reason to question the full-time director requisition
Quantifies the cost of this mistake using time-to-fill and ramp figures rather than asserting it generically
States that an aspirational hire is a risk to the hiring manager on multiple levels
States the profile-choice ordering out loud and names any options deleted by the answers given
Does not deliver a finished director-level role definition and interview loop as requested

evals.prompt: Here is the must-have list my CEO wrote for our RevOps Manager req at Pellworth Data - 110 people, Series B, analyst-leaning role at manager level: CRM administrator certification, marketing automation certification, 7+ years in RevOps, SQL, Python, Tableau, Looker, sales engagement tooling, conversation intelligence, CPQ, territory design, comp plan design, MBA preferred, startup experience, enterprise experience. Turn this into our requirements matrix and scoring sheet.
evals.expected_output: A requirements matrix capping must-haves at 5-7 weighted to 100%, the rest moved to additive nice-to-haves, disqualifiers held on a separate checklist, both certifications demoted because the archetype is analyst rather than systems, and experience scored level-relative.
expectations: Caps must-haves at between five and seven
Weights the must-haves so they sum to 100%
Moves the remaining requirements to nice-to-haves as additive bonus points outside the 100%
Holds disqualifiers on a separate checklist rather than as negative points inside the score
Flags that listing fifteen-plus requirements signals unrealistic expectations or a lack of role clarity
Rewrites the must-haves around problems rather than around named tools
Demotes both vendor certifications out of the must-haves because the archetype is analyst rather than systems
States that certifications are table stakes rather than predictors of performance
Scores the years-of-experience requirement level-relative and states that overqualified and underqualified both score low
Names SQL as the highest-leverage transferable technical skill because it survives a stack migration
Challenges the 7+ years requirement against a manager-level target rather than carrying it through unchanged
Produces a weighted table rather than an unordered list of requirements

evals.prompt: We're funding a Revenue Operations Manager req at Tindermoor, Series B, 160 people, based in Manchester with the option of remote anywhere in Europe. Finance approved GBP 62,000 base. Tell me whether that's right and give me the band I should be posting.
evals.expected_output: A statement that the quotable published bands are US-only and a refusal to invent a UK or European band, every figure carried with source and date, disagreeing sources shown rather than averaged, variable-pay structure and fully-loaded multiplier supplied, and the output labelled scoping input needing HR/legal review.
expectations: States that the published bands it can quote cover the US and declines to invent a UK or European band
Quotes every compensation figure with its source and its date
Presents at least two sources that disagree and shows the conflict rather than averaging them into a single number
Ranks source trust with survey-backed data above recruiter placement data above job-scrape or algorithmic estimates
Labels the compensation output as scoping input only and flags that offer terms need HR or legal review
States that RevOps variable pay is a target bonus tied to company performance rather than commission
Gives the variable share as roughly 5-10% of total for individual contributors and 15-25% at manager level and above
Applies a fully-loaded cost rule of thumb of base multiplied by roughly 1.30 to 1.40 plus equity
Labels the SF/NY/Boston premium and the narrowed remote discount as US figures rather than applying them to Manchester
Warns that underfunding the requisition produces either a struggling junior or a title the company cannot support
Recommends fighting for more money to hire an experienced professional rather than working with the money available and failing the new hire
Does not state a specific UK salary band as though it were sourced

evals.prompt: For our RevOps Analyst req at Corveth Labs we've built a take-home: we hand candidates our real anonymized pipeline export, ask for a full pipeline health analysis, a rebuilt stage model and a slide deck. We estimate eight hours. Unpaid. We're down to three finalists. Score it out of 100 and tell me how to grade it.
evals.expected_output: The eight-hour unpaid exercise deleted outright rather than shortened, the format ordering stated out loud, a two-hour cap with a three-hour unpaid ceiling, the paid format promoted because the finalist pool is three or fewer, a synthetic artifact substituted for the real export, and the summed score out of 100 replaced by a required-dimensions-at-bar rubric written before the first submission.
expectations: Deletes the eight-hour unpaid exercise outright rather than shortening or demoting it
States that a long unpaid exercise selects for uncommitted hours and that no rubric recovers the candidates it filtered out before submission
States the format ordering out loud: live mock above paid take-home above unpaid take-home on signal per hour spent
Names three hours as the ceiling for an unpaid exercise and roughly two hours as the working target
Flags the compliance cost of an unpaid exercise producing output the company could actually use
Notes that a take-home creates a candidate file the company must store, retain and be able to delete on request
Promotes the paid take-home because the finalist pool is three or fewer and the spend is therefore bounded
Replaces the real pipeline export with a small synthetic artifact
Requires the rubric to be written before the first submission arrives
Rejects a summed score out of 100 and instead requires every required dimension at the meets-bar anchor
Grades against the same anchored competency scale used in the interviews rather than a separate ad-hoc impression
Plans a structured debrief and states that the debrief carries more signal than the artifact
Recommends timing the exercise on the internal team first, noting candidates take roughly twice as long as the author

evals.prompt: Our RevOps Manager loop at Dunhollow runs six rounds: recruiter screen, hiring manager, CRO, VP Marketing, two AEs together, and a final with the CEO. After each round everyone drops a 1-5 rating on overall fit into a Slack channel and we talk it through in a group debrief. Both of our last two hires were whoever the CRO liked. Fix the loop.
evals.expected_output: A three-round loop plus one roughly two-hour take-home, a stage table with each competency owned by exactly one stage and each panelist in a lane, per-competency anchored scales with behavioral descriptions at every point, evidence-cited independent pre-scores, disqualifiers recorded separately, and confidence-weighted recommendations.
expectations: Cuts the loop to at most three rounds plus one take-home of about two hours
Produces a stage table mapping stage to interviewer to competencies assessed
Assigns each competency to exactly one stage
Assigns each panelist a lane rather than letting everyone probe everything
Replaces the single overall-fit rating with per-competency scoring
Writes a behavioral description of what each anchor point looks like for this specific role, not only the endpoints
States that a bare number or a generic label such as "Strong" fails the scoring standard
Requires every submitted score to cite a quote or a concrete example as evidence
Requires interviewers to submit scores independently before any discussion
Identifies scores shared before being written as the cause of converging on the first confident voice
Records disqualifying signals separately from the score
Weights the recommendation by fit and confidence together, and treats "insufficient data" as a valid output
Directs debrief time to where the scores diverged
States that no single score overrides the loop

evals.prompt: I'm building the interview questions for a Revenue Operations Manager at Wrenfold. It's a systems-heavy req - we're consolidating three CRMs into one and this hire owns that migration end to end. The panel is me (VP Sales), our head of marketing, and a senior AE. Give me the question set.
evals.expected_output: A question set with the discriminating-question ordering stated out loud, CRM data modelling promoted to first for a systems archetype but flagged because nobody on the named panel can grade it, the tool-first versus process-first filter named as highest yield, behavioral plus situational questions with probes per competency, domain probes ranked by rehearsability, and red/green anchors that differ in method.
expectations: States the discriminating-question ordering out loud rather than presenting a flat list
Promotes the CRM data-modelling question to first because the archetype is systems
Flags that nobody on the named panel is qualified to grade a data-model answer and requires adding a qualified grader or dropping the question
Names the tool-first versus process-first filter as the highest-yield signal and notes it consumes no dedicated interview minutes
Identifies a candidate whose first question about any problem is which tool to use as a red flag
Supplies two to three behavioral and one to two situational questions per competency
Attaches follow-up probes to the questions
Rejects leading questions and questions that bundle two questions into one
Builds at least one probe from a documented RevOps failure mode rather than from a generic behavioral bank
Ranks the domain probes by how hard they are to rehearse and places define-before-automate at the top
Asks the candidate what they would refuse to automate on day one
Supplies red/green answer pairs as scoring anchors where the weak and strong answers differ in method rather than in confidence
Treats commonly cited numbers such as pipeline coverage as prompts and scores whether the candidate questions their provenance

evals.prompt: Our new Director of Revenue Operations starts in 17 days at Astrelle Group. She's joining an existing four-person ops team and her mandate is cross-team process design plus owning the quarterly planning cadence. Write the 30-60-90. Our CEO wants forecast accuracy up 15 points by day 30.
evals.expected_output: A ramp plan branched on both seniority and archetype, the day-30 forecast target rejected against honest 60-90 day / 6-month / 12-month milestones, the strategist first deliverable and watch area, a light Day 1 with substantive ownership from Week 2, a non-manager buddy, a week-one access list, agreed ticket-queue protection, existing-team rather than greenfield sequencing, and a closing watch-areas section.
expectations: Rejects the day-30 forecast-accuracy target as an unrealistic milestone
Sets honest milestones: early wins at 60-90 days, structural improvements around six months, revenue-level outcomes at 12+ months
States that anyone promising revenue impact in 30 days is selling you something
Branches the plan on seniority and on archetype rather than on only one of them
Uses the strategist first deliverable: a stakeholder-interview synthesis and a process map of one revenue motion with a proposed operating cadence
Names the strategist watch area of strategy documents with no shipped change by day 60
Ends the plan with a watch-areas section distinct from the goals
Keeps Day 1 light and starts substantive ownership in Week 2
Assigns a buddy who is not the hiring manager
Includes a week-one access list covering CRM admin permissions, a CRM sandbox, data warehouse and BI access, the marketing automation platform, and seats in the pipeline and forecast meetings
Grants that access in week one rather than on request
Agrees with the sponsor before day one what share of time goes to the ticket queue and who absorbs the rest
Treats this as an existing-team ramp absorbing documented processes and standards rather than a greenfield diagnostic ramp
Writes the 30, 60 and 90 day goals from the role's ranked outcomes rather than generically

evals.prompt: Vessarine is a consumer subscription app - 2.1M free users, no sales team at all, just growth, product and support. We're hiring our first Revenue Operations Manager. I pulled a RevOps job description off a template site and it lists pipeline coverage, territory design, quota planning, CPQ and deal desk experience. Adapt it for us and build the competency set.
evals.expected_output: A packet stating the process is identical across segments while the weighting, metrics, stack and probes change; sales-led B2B requirements removed; PLG and consumer metrics substituted with any benchmark labelled directional; analytics-engineering skills weighted up; product-signal probes replacing territory design; and the B2B-marketing-specific domain probe deleted.
expectations: States that the hiring process itself - scorecard, loop, work sample, ramp - is identical across segments and that what changes is weighting, metrics, stack and probes
Removes territory design, quota planning and pipeline coverage as sales-led B2B concerns
Removes deal desk and CPQ, noting deal desk is close to a B2B-only archetype rarely present in consumer subscription
Names the metrics this role owns: activation, product-qualified leads, free-to-paid conversion and expansion signals
Includes consumer metrics such as CAC, conversion rate, average order value, purchase frequency, churn and cohort-modeled LTV
Labels any benchmark figures it cites as directional vendor-report numbers rather than authoritative
Gives activation as roughly 25-40% of signups within 7-14 days
Gives free-to-paid conversion as roughly 2-5% for freemium and 15-25% for free trial
Notes that PQL users convert around three times higher and that only about a quarter of PLG companies actually use PQLs
Weights analytics-engineering-adjacent skills: strong SQL, hands-on data-warehouse work and a transformation layer
Probes product-signal fluency instead of territory design in the interview
Deletes the revenue-team-alignment domain probe as B2B-marketing-specific rather than asking it thin
Notes that using funnel stages as a proxy for a team's effectiveness becomes nonsensical in PLG
Warns that pure B2C subscription usually lacks the expansion pathway that pushes B2B net retention above 100%

evals.prompt: Our board meets in 11 weeks and our forecast has been wrong three quarters running. Ferncastle, Series C, 240 people. I want to open a senior RevOps req this week and have that person present a fixed forecast process at the board meeting. Headcount is approved and our CFO will sponsor it. What level should I hire and how fast can we move?
evals.expected_output: A statement that a hard date inside a quarter deletes the senior in-house options, senior time-to-fill and time-to-productivity quoted, total calendar to first useful output used instead of time-to-fill alone, the junior-is-faster assumption rejected, a fractional or agency recommendation for the board date, and the one-off versus compounding question separated.
expectations: States that a hard date inside a quarter deletes the senior in-house options because the search alone outlasts the deadline
Quotes time to fill for a senior hire as roughly 12-16 weeks
Quotes time to productivity for a senior hire as roughly 1-3 months
Budgets against total calendar to first useful output rather than against time to fill alone
Rejects the assumption that a junior requisition is faster, noting junior time to productivity runs 4-6 months
Notes that mid and senior tie on total calendar because senior's extra search time buys back ramp time
Recommends a fractional operator or a scoped agency project to hit the eleven-week board date
Names the deleted options explicitly rather than ranking them last
Separates the one-off board-date fix from the compounding-capability question and routes each differently
States the ordering of the remaining options out loud
Confirms the executive sponsor and reporting line are locked in writing before the requisition opens
Does not promise that a senior in-house hire can present a fixed forecast process at the board in eleven weeks
